column1: How Dutch engineer Luud Schimmelpennink helped to devise urban bike-sharing schemes
column2: 荷兰工程师卢德·席默尔彭宁克如何参与构思城市共享单车计划。
column6: urban bike-sharing schemes|城市共享单车计划

column1: The original idea for an urban bike-sharing scheme dates back to a summer’s day in Amsterdam in 1965.
column2: 城市共享单车计划最初的构想，可以追溯到1965年阿姆斯特丹的一个夏日。

column1: Provo, the organisation that came up with the idea, was a group of Dutch activists who wanted to change society.
column2: 提出这一构想的是普罗沃组织。它由一群希望改变社会的荷兰活动人士组成。

column1: They believed the scheme, which was known as the Witte Fietsenplan, was an answer to the perceived threats of air pollution and consumerism.
column2: 他们把这个项目叫做“白色自行车计划”，认为它可以应对他们眼中空气污染和消费主义带来的威胁。

column1: In the centre of Amsterdam, they painted a small number of used bikes white.
column2: 他们在阿姆斯特丹市中心把少量旧自行车漆成了白色。

column1: They also distributed leaflets describing the dangers of cars and inviting people to use the white bikes.
column2: 他们还散发传单，说明汽车带来的危害，邀请人们骑这些白色自行车。

column1: The bikes were then left unlocked at various locations around the city, to be used by anyone in need of transport.
column2: 接着，他们把自行车放在城内各处，不上锁，任何需要交通工具的人都能取用。

column1: Luud Schimmelpennink, a Dutch industrial engineer who still lives and cycles in Amsterdam, was heavily involved in the original scheme.
column2: 荷兰工业工程师卢德·席默尔彭宁克至今仍在阿姆斯特丹生活和骑车。他当年深度参与了这项最早的计划。

column1: He recalls how the scheme succeeded in attracting a great deal of attention — particularly when it came to publicising Provo’s aims — but struggled to get off the ground.
column2: 他回忆说，这个计划成功吸引了大量关注，尤其让更多人知道了普罗沃的宗旨，但要让计划真正运转起来却很难。
column5: attracting a great deal of attention|吸引大量关注
column9: get off the ground|真正启动

column1: The police were opposed to Provo’s initiatives and almost as soon as the white bikes were distributed around the city, they removed them.
column2: 警方反对普罗沃的倡议。这些白色自行车刚分布到城内各处，警察几乎立刻就把车收走了。
column5: almost as soon as|几乎刚一……就

column1: However, for Schimmelpennink and for bike-sharing schemes in general, this was just the beginning.
column2: 然而，对席默尔彭宁克本人以及整个共享单车事业来说，这还只是个开端。

column1: ‘The first Witte Fietsenplan was just a symbolic thing,’ he says.
column2: “最初的白色自行车计划只是个象征。”他说。

column1: ‘We painted a few bikes white, that was all.
column2: “我们不过是把几辆自行车漆成白色，仅此而已。

column1: Things got more serious when I became a member of the Amsterdam city council two years later.’
column2: 两年后，我成了阿姆斯特丹市议会议员，事情这才认真做了起来。”
column3: got more serious|变得认真起来

column1: Schimmelpennink seized this opportunity to present a more elaborate Witte Fietsenplan to the city council.
column2: 席默尔彭宁克抓住这个机会，向市议会提交了一份更为详尽的白色自行车计划。

column1: ‘My idea was that the municipality of Amsterdam would distribute 10,000 white bikes over the city, for everyone to use,’ he explains.
column2: 他解释说：“我的想法是，由阿姆斯特丹市政府在全市投放一万辆白色自行车，供所有人使用。
column6: for everyone to use|供所有人使用

column1: ‘I made serious calculations.
column2: 我认真算过这笔账。

column1: It turned out that a white bicycle — per person, per kilometre — would cost the municipality only 10% of what it contributed to public transport per person per kilometre.’
column2: 结果发现，按每人每公里计算，白色自行车给市政府带来的成本，只相当于市政府按相同标准为公共交通投入资金的10%。”

column1: Nevertheless, the council unanimously rejected the plan.
column2: 尽管如此，市议会还是一致否决了这个计划。

column1: ‘They said that the bicycle belongs to the past.
column2: “他们说自行车属于过去。
column4: belongs to the past|已属于过去

column1: They saw a glorious future for the car,’ says Schimmelpennink.
column2: 在他们看来，汽车前途无量。”席默尔彭宁克说。

column1: But he was not in the least discouraged.
column2: 可他丝毫没有气馁。

column1: Schimmelpennink never stopped believing in bike-sharing, and in the mid-90s, two Danes asked for his help to set up a system in Copenhagen.
column2: 席默尔彭宁克始终相信共享单车行得通。20世纪90年代中期，两位丹麦人请他帮忙在哥本哈根建立一套系统。
column3: never stopped believing in|始终相信

column1: The result was the world’s first large-scale bike-share programme.
column2: 于是，世界上第一个大规模共享单车项目诞生了。

column1: It worked on a deposit: ‘You dropped a coin in the bike and when you returned it, you got your money back.’
column2: 它采用押金制：“你往自行车里投一枚硬币，还车时就能把钱取回来。”
column3: worked on a deposit|采用押金制
column4: dropped a coin in|往……里投一枚硬币
column6: got your money back|取回了押金

column1: After setting up the Danish system, Schimmelpennink decided to try his luck again in the Netherlands — and this time he succeeded in arousing the interest of the Dutch Ministry of Transport.
column2: 建成丹麦的系统后，席默尔彭宁克决定回荷兰再试一次。这次他成功引起了荷兰交通部的兴趣。
column7: arousing the interest of|引起……的兴趣

column1: ‘Times had changed,’ he recalls.
column2: “时代已经变了。”他回忆说。

column1: ‘People had become more environmentally conscious, and the Danish experiment had proved that bike-sharing was a real possibility.’
column2: “人们的环保意识增强了，而且丹麦的试验也证明，共享单车确实可行。”

column1: A new Witte Fietsenplan was launched in 1999 in Amsterdam.
column2: 1999年，阿姆斯特丹推出了一项新的白色自行车计划。

column1: However, riding a white bike was no longer free; it cost one guilder per trip and payment was made with a chip card developed by the Dutch bank Postbank.
column2: 不过，这次骑白色自行车不再免费，每骑一次要花一荷兰盾，车费通过荷兰邮政银行开发的芯片卡支付。

column1: Schimmelpennink designed conspicuous, sturdy white bikes locked in special racks which could be opened with the chip card — the plan started with 250 bikes, distributed over five stations.
column2: 席默尔彭宁克设计的白色自行车醒目又结实，锁在专用车架上，刷芯片卡便能开锁。计划启动时共有250辆车，分布在五个站点。

column1: Theo Molenaar, who was a system designer for the project, worked alongside Schimmelpennink.
column2: 特奥·莫勒纳尔是这个项目的系统设计师，和席默尔彭宁克共事。

column1: ‘I remember when we were testing the bike racks, he announced that he had already designed better ones.
column2: “我记得，我们还在测试停车架时，他就宣布自己已经设计出了更好的。

column1: But of course, we had to go through with the ones we had.’
column2: 可我们当然还是得用现有的车架把项目做下去。”
column5: the ones we had|我们手头已有的车架

column1: The system, however, was prone to vandalism and theft.
column2: 然而，这套系统很容易遭到蓄意破坏，车辆也很容易失窃。

column1: ‘After every weekend there would always be a couple of bikes missing,’ Molenaar says.
column2: “每个周末一过，总会少上两三辆车。”莫勒纳尔说。
column3: After every weekend|每个周末过后

column1: ‘I really have no idea what people did with them, because they could instantly be recognised as white bikes.’
column2: “我真不知道人们把车弄去干什么，因为一眼就能认出它们是白色自行车。”

column1: But the biggest blow came when Postbank decided to abolish the chip card, because it wasn’t profitable.
column2: 但打击最大的是，邮政银行认为芯片卡无利可图，决定停用这种卡。

column1: ‘That chip card was pivotal to the system,’ Molenaar says.
column2: “那张芯片卡是这套系统运作的关键。”莫勒纳尔说。

column1: ‘To continue the project we would have needed to set up another system, but the business partner had lost interest.’
column2: “要继续开展这个项目，我们就得另建一套系统，但我们的商业伙伴已经失去了兴趣。”
column4: would have needed to|当时本来需要

column1: Schimmelpennink was disappointed, but — characteristically — not for long.
column2: 席默尔彭宁克很失望，但按他一贯的性格，这种失望并没有持续多久。
column5: not for long|没有持续太久

column1: In 2002 he got a call from the French advertising corporation JC Decaux, who wanted to set up his bike-sharing scheme in Vienna.
column2: 2002年，他接到法国广告公司德高集团的电话，对方想在维也纳推行他的共享单车方案。

column1: ‘That went really well.
column2: “事情进展得非常顺利。
column3: went really well|进展非常顺利

column1: After Vienna, they set up a system in Lyon.
column2: 继维也纳之后，他们又在里昂建立了一套系统。

column1: Then in 2007, Paris followed.
column2: 随后在2007年，巴黎也跟了上来。

column1: That was a decisive moment in the history of bike-sharing.’
column2: 那是共享单车史上的一个决定性时刻。”

column1: The huge and unexpected success of the Parisian bike-sharing programme, which now boasts more than 20,000 bicycles, inspired cities all over the world to set up their own schemes, all modelled on Schimmelpennink’s.
column2: 巴黎共享单车项目取得了出人意料的巨大成功，如今已有两万多辆自行车。这促使世界各地的城市纷纷推出自己的方案，都是以席默尔彭宁克的设计为蓝本。
column8: all over the world|世界各地

column1: ‘It’s wonderful that this happened,’ he says.
column2: “能有这样的结果，真是太好了。”他说。

column1: ‘But financially I didn’t really benefit from it, because I never filed for a patent.’
column2: “不过在经济上，我其实没从中得到什么好处，因为我从来没有申请过专利。”
column5: filed for a patent|申请专利

column1: In Amsterdam today, 38% of all trips are made by bike and, along with Copenhagen, it is regarded as one of the two most cycle-friendly capitals in the world — but the city never got another Witte Fietsenplan.
column2: 如今，阿姆斯特丹38%的出行是骑自行车完成的。它和哥本哈根被视为世界上两个最适合骑行的首都，但阿姆斯特丹一直没有再推出白色自行车计划。

column1: Molenaar believes this may be because everybody in Amsterdam already has a bike.
column2: 莫勒纳尔认为，这或许是因为阿姆斯特丹人已经人手一辆自行车。

column1: Schimmelpennink, however, cannot see that this changes Amsterdam’s need for a bike-sharing scheme.
column2: 但席默尔彭宁克认为，这一点并没有改变阿姆斯特丹对共享单车计划的需要。

column1: ‘People who travel on the underground don’t carry their bikes around.
column2: “乘地铁的人不会随身带着自己的自行车。
column3: travel on the underground|乘地铁出行
column4: carry their bikes around|到处带着自己的自行车

column1: But often they need additional transport to reach their final destination.’
column2: 但他们下了地铁，常常还需要其他交通工具才能到达最终目的地。”

column1: Although he thinks it is strange that a city like Amsterdam does not have a successful bike-sharing scheme, he is optimistic about the future.
column2: 在他看来，像阿姆斯特丹这样的城市竟然没有成功的共享单车方案，的确很奇怪，但他对未来很乐观。

column1: ‘In the ‘60s we didn’t stand a chance because people were prepared to give their lives to keep cars in the city.
column2: “在20世纪60年代，我们没有丝毫胜算，因为人们宁可豁出性命也要让汽车留在城里。
column3: stand a chance|有成功的希望
column6: keep cars in the city|让汽车留在城内

column1: But that mentality has totally changed.
column2: 然而，那种心态已经彻底变了。

column1: Today everybody longs for cities that are not dominated by cars.’
column2: 如今，人人都盼望城市不再由汽车主宰。”
